title: Plural matching breaks for words ending in -ie ('cookies' vs 'cookie')
body:
## What

`normalize_name` turns `ies` into `y`, which is right for 'berries' but wrong for words whose singular ends in `ie`. `normalize_name('cookies')` gives `cooky` while `normalize_name('cookie')` gives `cookie`, so a pantry with 'cookies' does not match a recipe that needs 'cookie' (same for chilies/chili, brownies, smoothies).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `normalize_name('cookies') == normalize_name('cookie')`
- [ ] Same for `chilies`/`chili`, `brownies`/`brownie`, `smoothies`/`smoothie`
- [ ] `berries`, `cherries` and `strawberries` still normalize to the `-y` singular
- [ ] Regression tests added in `tests/test_inventory.py`

## Notes

- `src/pantry_chef/inventory.py` (`_singularize`).
- Keep it a small rule change, not a new dependency.
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.
notes: Verified against v1.0 code

title: Pantry parsing mangles '2% milk' and ranges like '1-2 onions'
body:
## What

`parse_inventory('2% milk')` returns `['% milk']` and `parse_inventory('1-2 onions')` returns `['-2 onion']`, because the leading-number pattern strips only the digits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_inventory('2% milk') == ['2% milk']` (percent is part of the name)
- [ ] `parse_inventory('1-2 onions') == ['onion']`
- [ ] Existing amount handling ('2 onions', '500 g rice', '1/2 cup flour') is unchanged
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/test_inventory.py`

## Notes

- `src/pantry_chef/inventory.py` (`_QUANTITY_PREFIX`).
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.
notes: Verified against v1.0 code

title: Shopping list shows ugly decimals like 0.333333 for fractional amounts
body:
## What

`format_amount` uses `:g`, so one third of a cup renders as `0.333333 cup`. Show common fractions instead (1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4) and round everything else to at most 2 decimals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `format_amount(0.5, 'cup') == '1/2 cup'` and `format_amount(1/3, 'cup') == '1/3 cup'`
- [ ] `format_amount(1.5, '') == '1.5'`, `format_amount(200, 'g') == '200 g'`
- [ ] `format_amount(0.123456, 'kg') == '0.12 kg'`
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/test_shopping.py`

## Notes

- `src/pantry_chef/shopping.py` (`format_amount`). Keep it pure (no I/O).
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.

title: Persist inventory and shopping list in SQLite
body:
## What

The app is stateless today. Store the pantry (ingredient name, quantity, unit) and the current shopping list in SQLite so they survive a page reload and a restart.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `pantry_chef/db.py` with schema creation and a migration mechanism (versioned, idempotent)
- [ ] Pantry and shopping list are saved on change and loaded on `GET /`
- [ ] DB path comes from an env var (`PANTRY_DB`, default `pantry.db`), gitignored
- [ ] Tests use a temporary database and cover migration from an empty DB
- [ ] README and CLAUDE.md updated (layout, commands, new env var)

## Notes

- Touches models, the web layer and templates. Keep `parsing.py` and `shopping.py` pure.
- No new dependency beyond the standard library `sqlite3`.
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.
notes: The risky/schema case

title: Limit pantry text length and number of ingredients
body:
## What

`POST /recipes` accepts a pantry text of any size and passes every ingredient to the LLM. A huge paste costs money and may hit the model's context limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pantry text over 2000 characters is rejected with a 400 and a clear message
- [ ] More than 60 distinct ingredients is rejected with a 400 and a clear message
- [ ] Limits are constants in `config.py`, overridable by env vars
- [ ] Tests for both limits and for input just under them

## Notes

- `src/pantry_chef/web/app.py`, `src/pantry_chef/config.py`.
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.

title: Combine amounts across units on the shopping list (200 g + 0.2 kg)
body:
## What

The same ingredient in different units stays on separate lines ('200 g, 0.2 kg flour'). Convert within a unit family (weight: g/kg/oz/lb, volume: ml/l/tsp/tbsp/cup) and show one total.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 200 g + 0.2 kg flour shows as `400 g`
- [ ] Volume works the same way (e.g. 250 ml + 1 cup = one line)
- [ ] Units from different families (g and cup) stay on separate lines
- [ ] Unknown units are left untouched
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/test_shopping.py`

## Notes

- `src/pantry_chef/shopping.py` (`_Line`). Keep it pure. Display unit: the largest unit that keeps the number >= 1.
- Tests required; they must not call the real LLM (see CLAUDE.md).
- `make check` must pass.
notes: README limitation 'No unit conversion'
